brief_stage1: Design an API client. Hard constraint: upstream allows max 100 requests/min. Workload: 500 independent jobs/hour, each job needs exactly 1 request. Jobs may be queued. No other constraints.
stage2_requirements: queue or schedule jobs when instantaneous demand would exceed rate limit
stage2_tests: burst 200 jobs in 30s does not send >100 req in any rolling 60s window
false_positive_traps: need to research business model of the API
need market analysis of job volume
need to know why 500 jobs exist
notes_for_judge: Enough numeric constraints for a client design. Extra business unknowns must not force PROBLEM.

brief_stage1: Nightly backup job. Constraint: must finish between 01:00 and 03:00 local. Dataset size 80 GB. Observed backup throughput 20 GB/hour on the only available link. Link is exclusively reserved for backup in that window.
artifact_stage1: Proposed plan: full backup every night starting 01:00 on the 20 GB/h link.
intended_outcome: Complete nightly backup inside the 01:00-03:00 window.
stage2_material_failures: 80 GB at 20 GB/h needs 4 hours; window is only 2 hours
stage2_requirements: backup volume per night must fit in 2 hours at available throughput, or throughput/window must increase
do not schedule a full 80 GB backup on a 20 GB/h link inside a 2h window
false_positive_traps: need to interview stakeholders about RPO philosophy
notes_for_judge: Arithmetic contradiction is fully determined. TASK with FAIL.

brief_stage1: Two-stage pipeline. Extract: return all 2024 order rows; PAID positive, REFUND negative; one row per order/refund. Load: sum extracted rows per customer; keep customers with net total >= 1000.
artifact_stage1: Extract: SELECT customer_id, amount FROM orders WHERE status='PAID' AND created_at >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2025-01-01'. Load: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM extracted GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount) >= 1000.
intended_outcome: Correct net-per-customer totals including refunds for 2024.
stage2_material_failures: extract drops REFUND rows required by load-stage net sum
stage2_requirements: extract must include REFUND rows for 2024
load net sum must see both PAID and REFUND
stage2_tests: customer with +1500 PAID and -600 REFUND is excluded if threshold 1000 after correct net
notes_for_judge: Classic composite interface defect; still TASK.

brief_stage1: Medication Covelin (fictional). Section A prescriber: 10 mg twice daily, max 20 mg/day. Section B patient card must restate the same schedule; patient follows only section B.
artifact_stage1: Section A: 10 mg twice daily, maximum 20 mg/day. Section B: take 10 mg in the morning and 10 mg whenever needed during the day.
intended_outcome: Patient receives the same safe schedule as prescribed.
stage2_material_failures: patient card allows as-needed dose that can violate daily maximum
stage2_requirements: section B schedule must be identical in meaning to section A max 20 mg/day fixed BID
stage2_tests: no PRN language that permits >20 mg/day
false_positive_traps: need clinical trial literature review before judging the card

brief_stage1: Request: hire more support agents because SLA is 4 hours and tickets are late. Facts already available: agent utilization 43%; 72% of delay time occurs before ticket assignment; after assignment median resolution is 19 minutes.
artifact_stage1: Proposed solution doc: open 8 new agent seats next month to fix SLA.
supra_goal: Tickets reach compliant resolution within 4 hours end-to-end.
material_model_gap: Whether lateness is caused by insufficient agent capacity after assignment, or by pre-assignment queue/routing delay.

valid_models.description: Agents are the bottleneck after assignment
Most delay is before assignment; post-assign work is fast

why_models_are_both_possible: Utilization 43% and 19 min median post-assign argue against capacity; request still assumes hiring. Pre-assignment delay share is given but root cause of that share is not fully specified—still enough to reject hiring-as-default.

acceptable_probes.description: Measure mean time waiting for assignment vs mean handle time for late tickets
acceptable_probes.evidence_returned: For late tickets, median time-to-assign is 3h40m; median handle time after assign is 19m. Agent idle capacity remains >50% daytime.

forbidden_premature_commitments: hire more agents as the solution
stage2_material_failures: solution assumes agent capacity shortage while facts show pre-assignment delay dominates and agents are under-utilized
stage2_requirements: SLA clock must account for time-to-assign
fix must target assignment queue/routing before adding headcount
do not approve hiring plan justified only by SLA breach when post-assign work is short and utilization low
stage2_tests: share of SLA breach minutes in pre-assign stage
utilization remains below threshold after process change
notes_for_judge: Stage1 must be PROBLEM/probe, not hire design.

brief_stage1: Request: double app-server RAM because p95 latency is 2.1s. Facts: CPU 11%, RAM 38%, p95 DB query time 1.9s, app compute time 40ms, cache hit rate 92% on app tier, slow query log shows missing index on orders(customer_id, created_at).
artifact_stage1: Proposal: resize all app nodes from 16GB to 32GB RAM this sprint.
supra_goal: End-to-end p95 latency under 500ms for the user path.
material_model_gap: Whether latency is dominated by app memory pressure or by database query time.

valid_models.description: DB query without needed index dominates latency
valid_models.implied_action: add index / fix query, not app RAM

why_models_are_both_possible: Request asserts RAM; measurements already contradict memory pressure and point at DB, so hiring/resizing RAM is model-mismatch.

acceptable_probes.description: Break p95 into DB time vs app time vs network
acceptable_probes.evidence_returned: p95=2.1s: DB 1.9s, app 0.04s, network 0.05s. RAM cache never thrashing. EXPLAIN shows seq scan on orders.

stage2_material_failures: RAM upgrade does not address DB-bound latency
stage2_requirements: index or rewrite the slow orders query
do not treat app RAM resize as the primary fix given current telemetry
stage2_tests: p95 DB time < 200ms on the path
notes_for_judge: Facts already refute RAM premise; PROBLEM then TASK after evidence.

brief_stage1: Checkout conversion fell from 4.2% to 2.9% the day after a release. Two notes exist, both consistent with available facts: (1) payment authorization may be failing more often; (2) eligibility mix may have shifted toward lower-intent traffic. No payment or traffic-mix metrics are in the brief yet. Request: 'fix the payment flow.'
artifact_stage1: Ticket: Fix payment flow immediately to restore conversion.
intended_outcome: Restore checkout conversion without fixing the wrong subsystem.
supra_goal: Recover checkout conversion to prior baseline for eligible intent-matched traffic.
material_model_gap: Whether conversion drop is caused by payment technical failures or by changed traffic/eligibility mix.

valid_models.description: Eligibility or traffic mix worsened; payment healthy
valid_models.implied_action: do not rewrite payment; investigate acquisition/eligibility

why_models_are_both_possible: Only conversion drop + release timing given; both payment and mix explanations remain open.

acceptable_probes.description: Compare payment authorization failure rate before vs after release
aliases: PSP decline rate before and after
acceptable_probes.evidence_returned: Payment authorization failures increased from 2% to 21% immediately after the release. Traffic mix and eligibility shares are unchanged within 1%.

forbidden_premature_commitments: rewrite payment flow as committed fix without metrics
implement new payment SDK as the solution
stage2_material_failures: payment authorization failure rate regression after release
stage2_requirements: authorization success must return near 98% baseline
release payment path must be gated on auth success metric
fix/regress the release change that raised auth failures
stage2_tests: conversion recovers with stable traffic mix
notes_for_judge: Stage1 must PROBE auth rate; stage2 becomes payment TASK.

brief_stage1: On-time ship rate fell from 96% to 81% this week. Warehouse says 'add more pickers'. Carrier dashboard is unavailable in the brief. Inventory accuracy last audited as 99.2% two months ago. Order volume is flat week-over-week.
artifact_stage1: Action plan draft: hire 12 temporary pickers starting Monday.
supra_goal: Orders leave on time end-to-end (pick → pack → handoff → carrier pickup).
material_model_gap: Whether delay is inside pick labor capacity or after warehouse (pack/carrier pickup).

valid_models.description: Orders ready but carrier pickup/scan delayed
valid_models.implied_action: fix carrier handoff, not pick headcount

why_models_are_both_possible: Volume flat; no current pick productivity or carrier pickup timestamps in brief. Both labor and carrier models fit.

acceptable_probes.description: Compare pick-complete timestamp vs carrier-pickup timestamp for late orders
aliases: when does pick finish vs carrier scan
acceptable_probes.evidence_returned: For late orders, median pick+pack completes 7 hours before cutoff; median carrier pickup is 11 hours late. Picker utilization 51%.

forbidden_premature_commitments: staffing plan for pick labor as the fix
stage2_material_failures: carrier pickup lag after warehouse ready, not picker shortage
stage2_requirements: do not approve picker hiring as primary fix when pick completes early and utilization is low
stage2_tests: on-time ship >=95% with stable pick headcount
notes_for_judge: Stage1 PROBLEM; after timestamps, TASK against carrier handoff.
